text.p: There is a Kennedy on the Dole campaign team but it is the frizzy-haired, bespectacled MTV host, no relation to the Democratic political clan.

Kennedy, the one-named cable channel star, has joined Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole on the road for his final non-stop campaign push. She is part of the celebrity retinue with Dole to help fire up crowds as he storms through 19 states in 96 hours with his voice close to giving out.

They also include golfer Chi Chi Rodriguez, who said he would never call President Bill Clinton "Mr. President" because Clinton avoided the draft; actress Bo Derek, who did not say anything, and country music stalwarts, the Oak Ridge Boys, who sing to their taped band.
Kennedy's contribution is encouraging the youth vote. Here are some examples of her rhetoric as she attempts to bridge the gap between the generation of Dole, 73, and Generation-X:

At a midnight rally in Sacramento -- "Bill the Chump is not welcome in D.C. any more. He does not have your best interests in mind. He does not have a heart, and frankly, I think he's unethical ... Send Bubba packing."
At a diner in Phoenix, before dawn -- "I've always fantasized about thousands of people in front of a diner ... I say to you, let them eat pancakes."

At the Space Centre in Alamogordo -- "I see a man right here wearing a hat that says 'politically incorrect,' and one of the most politically incorrect things I can think of in this election is counting out the youth vote. Never count out the youth vote in any election.
"So whether you're young, or old, conservative, or just kind of conservative, get out there tomorrow and vote, encourage everyone you know to vote, or I'll get your goat."
